title: Grade 4 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — 6.1 Obligations of Parents to Children

pages.lesson:
PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

Parents have duties towards their children. Islam calls these duties an amanah, a trust from Allah (S.W.T.). In this sub-strand you will state what parents owe their children, see why those duties matter, and recognise the love and care you receive at home.

## Strand 6.0: Muamalaat (Social Relations)
Sub-strand 6.1: Obligations of Parents to Children
Suggested lessons: 2

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) state the obligations of parents to their children
b) assess the importance of parents fulfilling their obligations towards their children
c) demonstrate ways in which parents can fulfil their obligations to their children
d) cherish love and care given to them by their parents

## Key inquiry questions
1. What are some of the things parents do for their children?
2. Why is it important for parents to fulfil their obligation towards their children?

## Core competencies
• Communication and collaboration: the skill of writing and teamwork as learners discuss parents’ obligations towards their children, in pairs/ small groups, and write the points in their notebook.
• Digital literacy: the skill of interacting with technology as learners watch/listen anashid from digital devices on the roles of parents to their children.
• Critical thinking and problem solving is enhanced as learners discuss the importance of parents fulfilling their obligations towards their children and present in class.
• Self-efficacy: the skill of personal skill is enhanced as learners role-play obligations of parents towards their children.

## Values
• Social justice enhanced as learners discuss the importance of parents fulfilling their obligations towards their children in and present in class
• Responsibility enhanced as learners role-play the obligations of parents to their children

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Citizenship: Child’s right to get education, shelter, and medical care.
• Socio-economic issues: Care and protection from parents to enhance safety and security of the children.

## Links to other learning areas
• Social Studies: as learners discuss the rights and responsibilities of citizens.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Islamic Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 6.0 Muamalaat (Social Relations), Sub-strand 6.1 Obligations of Parents to Children
• Qur'an 66:6
• Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim: each of you is a shepherd; be just among your children

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: What parents owe their children

LESSON 1: WHAT PARENTS OWE THEIR CHILDREN
=========================================

## What you will learn
• State the obligations of parents to their children.
• Give examples of each obligation in daily life.
• Recognise parental care as a trust from Allah.

Curriculum outcomes: a) state the obligations of parents to their children; d) cherish love and care given to them by their parents

## Introduction
Before you were old enough to feed yourself, someone fed you, dressed you and kept you safe. Those actions are not favours that can be ignored. In Islam they are obligations.

## Notes
### Parents are responsible
The Prophet (S.A.W) said that each of you is a shepherd and each of you is responsible for his flock. A man is responsible for his family, and a woman is responsible for the home (Bukhari and Muslim). Children are part of that trust.

Allah also commands believers to protect themselves and their families from the Fire (Qur'an 66:6). Parents do this by teaching Islam and by meeting the child's needs.

### Obligations of parents
- A good name: a parent gives the child a good name with a good meaning.
- Food and clothing: enough halal food, and clothes that cover the body and suit the weather.
- Shelter: a safe place to sleep and live.
- Medical care: treatment when the child is sick, and care that prevents illness where the family can provide it.
- Education: school learning and Islamic learning, including the Qur'an, swalah and good manners.
- Love and kindness: gentle words, time, and fairness between children. The Prophet (S.A.W) told a father to be just among his children (Bukhari and Muslim).
- Protection: keeping children away from harm, dangerous places and people who would hurt them.
- Religious upbringing: showing them how to pray, fast when they are able, and tell the truth.

### Cherishing this care
Many of these duties happen quietly: a parent waking early to prepare breakfast, paying school costs, or sitting with a sick child. A Muslim child notices this care and thanks Allah for it, even when the family has little. Not every family can provide the same things, but the duty to try, and to be fair and kind, remains.

## Key words
• obligation — a duty that a person ought to fulfil
• amanah — a trust that must be looked after
• shepherd — in the Hadith, a person who is responsible for those under his or her care

## Worked examples

### Example 1
A father pays school fees for one child and refuses to send the other child to school, though he can afford both. Which obligation is he failing, and which teaching has he forgotten?

Working:
1. Education is a right and an obligation.
2. The Prophet (S.A.W) commanded justice among children.

Answer: He is failing the duty of education and the duty of fairness.

## Activity: Parents' duties on paper
You will need: Exercise book
1. In pairs or small groups, brainstorm parents' obligations towards their children.
2. Write the points in your notebook under headings such as food, shelter, education, health, love and religion.
3. Next to each point, write one real example from family life, without naming private problems.
4. Share two points with the class.

## Practice
1. State five obligations of parents to their children.
2. What does the Hadith of the shepherd teach parents?
3. Why should parents treat their children justly?
4. Name two ways parents protect their children.

## Summary
• Parents are shepherds of their children and will be asked about that trust.
• Children are owed food, clothing, shelter, health care, education, love, protection and religious guidance.
• Fairness between children is part of that duty.

### Answers to practice
1. Any five: a good name, food, clothing, shelter, medical care, education, love and kindness, protection, religious upbringing, fairness.
2. Each person is responsible for those under his or her care, including the family.
3. The Prophet (S.A.W) commanded fairness among children, and injustice hurts love in the family.
4. Any two: providing safe shelter, keeping them from harm, teaching them, seeking treatment when they are sick, guiding them in Islam.

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: Why these obligations matter, and how parents fulfil them

LESSON 2: WHY THESE OBLIGATIONS MATTER, AND HOW PARENTS FULFIL THEM
============================================================

## What you will learn
• Explain the importance of parents fulfilling their obligations.
• Show, through examples, how parents carry out these duties.
• Express appreciation for the care given by parents.

Curriculum outcomes: b) assess the importance of parents fulfilling their obligations towards their children; c) demonstrate ways in which parents can fulfil their obligations to their children; d) cherish love and care given to them by their parents

## Introduction
A child who is fed, taught and kept safe can grow into a useful person. When those duties are ignored, the child suffers, and the whole community feels the result.

## Notes
### Why the obligations are important
- The child stays alive and healthy. Food, clothes, shelter and medicine are the base of life.
- The child learns. Education, both in school and in Islam, opens a future and protects the child from ignorance.
- The child feels loved and secure. Love and fairness build confidence and good character.
- The child learns to worship Allah. A home that teaches swalah and honesty raises a person who benefits society.
- Parents themselves succeed. Fulfilling the trust is obedience to Allah. Neglecting it is a failure they will be asked about.
- Society becomes safer. A child who is cared for is less likely to be lost, hurt or pushed into wrong ways. Care and protection from parents support the safety of children.

### How parents fulfil the duties
- They work lawfully to provide food, clothing, shelter and school needs.
- They take a sick child for treatment and follow advice on rest and medicine.
- They teach swalah by praying where the child can see, and they answer questions about Islam.
- They listen, correct with kindness, and avoid favouring one child over another.
- They know where the child is and who the child's friends are.
- They choose a good name and use it with respect.

### What children should feel
Children cannot pay parents back fully, but they can cherish the care: notice it, thank the parent, make dua for them, and not waste what is provided. Anashid about parents remind us of this love. If a family is poor, the child still values the effort, and the community may help with education and care. The obligation is to do what one is able to do, with sincerity.

## Key words
• fulfil — to carry out a duty completely
• upbringing — the way a child is raised and taught
• anashid — Islamic songs, often used here to praise the role of parents

## Worked examples

### Example 1
During a role-play, a mother finds her child has a high fever at night. List three actions that fulfil her obligations.

Working:
1. Medical care: seek help and give the right care.
2. Comfort: stay with the child.
3. Dua: ask Allah for healing.

Answer: She checks the fever, seeks treatment, comforts the child and makes dua.

## Activity: Role-play: a parent's day
You will need: Simple props such as a book, a plate and a scarf, A recording of anashid on parents if a digital device is available
1. Discuss in groups why it is important for parents to fulfil their obligations, then present two reasons to the class.
2. Role-play three short scenes: a parent helping with homework, a parent taking a child for treatment, and a parent teaching swalah.
3. After each scene, the class names the obligation that was shown.
4. If a device is available, listen to a short nashid on the role of parents and write one line you remember. Then write a short thank-you dua for your parents.

## Practice
1. Give three reasons why it is important for parents to fulfil their obligations.
2. State two ways a parent can fulfil the duty of education.
3. How can a child show that he or she cherishes parental care?

## Summary
• Parental duties keep children healthy, educated, loved and guided in Islam.
• Parents fulfil them by providing, teaching, protecting and being fair.
• Children cherish this care by thanking their parents and making dua for them.

### Answers to practice
1. Any three: the child stays healthy; the child is educated; the child feels loved and safe; the child learns Islam; parents obey Allah; society becomes safer.
2. Any two: sending the child to school, teaching the Qur'an and swalah, helping with learning at home, paying school costs when able.
3. By thanking them, making dua for them, obeying them and not wasting what they provide.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 6.1 OBLIGATIONS OF PARENTS TO CHILDREN
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Why is a parent compared to a shepherd in the Hadith?
   A. parents keep sheep only
   B. parents are responsible for their family
   C. children never need care
   D. work is forbidden

2. Which of these is an obligation of parents?
   A. Buying every toy in the shop
   B. Providing food, shelter and education
   C. Letting children do anything they like
   D. Favouring one child and ignoring another

3. According to Qur'an 66:6, believers should protect themselves and their families from which of these?
   A. the market
   B. the Fire
   C. school
   D. travel

4. Being just among children means…

5. Why is education an important parental duty?
   A. It is only for showing off
   B. It protects the child from ignorance and prepares a lawful future
   C. Children do not need to learn Islam
   D. School replaces all kindness

6. A parent who seeks treatment for a sick child is fulfilling which duty?
   A. medical care
   B. trade
   C. fashion
   D. travel

7. Which action shows a parent teaching religion?
   A. Hiding the prayer mat
   B. Praying where the child can learn swalah
   C. Stopping the child from saying Bismillah
   D. Laughing at the Qur'an

8. Why should children cherish the care their parents give?

9. How can a child respond to parental care?
   A. Waste food and mock them
   B. Thank them and make dua for them
   C. Ignore them
   D. Demand what the family cannot afford

10. Give one reason society benefits when parents protect and educate their children.
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 6.1 OBLIGATIONS OF PARENTS TO CHILDREN
========================================

1. B. parents are responsible for their family
   The Prophet (S.A.W) said each person is responsible for those under his or her care.

2. B. Providing food, shelter and education
   Basic care and education are duties. Favouritism is against the teaching of justice.

3. B. the Fire
   Parents protect the family by teaching faith and meeting their duties.

4. Treating them fairly and not favouring one over another without right.
   The Prophet (S.A.W) commanded a father to fear Allah and be just among his children.

5. B. It protects the child from ignorance and prepares a lawful future
   Both school learning and Islamic learning are part of a child's upbringing.

6. A. medical care
   Health care is one of the child's rights and the parent's obligations.

7. B. Praying where the child can learn swalah
   Children learn worship by being taught and by seeing it practised.

8. Because that care is a trust carried out for them, often with effort and love, and it helps them grow.
   Noticing and thanking parents is part of good character.

9. B. Thank them and make dua for them
   Gratitude and dua show that the child values the obligation the parents fulfil.

10. Children grow up safer, more useful and less likely to be harmed or left without guidance.
   Care at home supports safety and good citizenship.
